_comment: Shared destructive-git-guard corpus (AC-K1-1). Vendored byte-identical into codex-ai-harness at the pin in hooks/UPSTREAM. setup_ops below is the CLOSED vocabulary hooks/test_destructive_git_cases.py accepts -- an op name outside this set fails the suite (AC-SEC-5).

setup_ops.init: git init the fixture directory on branch `branch` (default "master")
setup_ops.write: write `content` to `path` without staging or committing it (creating parent directories as needed) -- dirty if `path` is already tracked, untracked otherwise
setup_ops.gitignore: write and commit a .gitignore file containing one line per entry of `patterns`
setup_ops.nested_repo: git init a SEPARATE repository inside `path` (creating it if needed), with its own committed-then-dirtied tracked file, independent of the outer fixture repo
setup_ops.stash_push: run `git stash push` for real against the fixture's current dirty state, leaving one genuine stash entry and a clean working tree
setup_ops.branch: create a branch named `name` off the current HEAD, without switching to it
setup_ops.config: set the repository-local git config `key` to `value` (repo config, so it overrides whatever the developer's global config happens to say -- the point of every case that uses it)

AC-QA-2 (round 4, M5): the allow twin for every `stash push then drop` case is IMPOSSIBLE and this records why, rather than leaving the shape half-covered. Whether a push creates an entry depends on the tree at RUN time, which this guard would have to measure separately and could still lose a race on, so it assumes the push succeeds and fails CLOSED. cases.command: echo stash@{0} | xargs git stash drop stash@{5}
cases.note: AC-ARCH-4 (round 4, M3): the only shape in which stash's conservative reading of UNKNOWN trailing arguments changes the answer, and it is here so that reading is observable rather than merely asserted. A ref IS on the command line (stash@{5}, which names no existing entry, so on its own it would be allowed) and xargs appends another the guard cannot see, so any entry could be the one dropped and the drop is read as a clear. Recorded honestly: git itself rejects two revisions (`Too many revisions specified`, measured), so this is a refusal on a malformed command. Every well-formed xargs-fed drop leaves the ref off the command line entirely, where it already defaults to stash@{0} and blocks whenever the list is non-empty

(round 4, M4, no AC -- spec bug) a command substitution runs in its own child process at the point its SEGMENT runs, so it sees every earlier segment's `cd`. (round 4, M4) the counterweight to the two cases above: a stash PUSH is a repo-global fact, not a process-local one, so it must still be visible to a later outer segment even though the push happened inside a child process.
